dominant_strengths: Restrained dark palette with single blue accent reads cleanly and avoids visual clutter on a tracking surface
Decay through label opacity is a legible signal — older items literally fade, intent is communicated
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty canvas below five short rows breaks composition; the timeline feels abandoned, not intentional whitespace
Age-decay system is one-dimensional: only label opacity dims while bar color, thickness, and dot stay identical, weakening the metaphor
Right-side duration labels (1h, 2h, 8h, 3d, 5d) sit detached with no visual hierarchy tying them to bar length or decay state
fix_priorities: Layer the decay: desaturate bar hue, soften dot, and reduce stroke weight in tandem with label opacity for a true age gradient
Compress vertical rhythm or fill the canvas with secondary context (heatmap, scrubber, week markers) so the timeline owns its space
Tie duration labels into the decay system with matched opacity and tabular numerics for scannable hierarchy
Introduce a subtle temporal axis or gridline so 1h vs 5d has spatial meaning, not just textual
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral legibility is adequate but visceral pull is thin and reflective payoff is missing — it informs without resonating.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the age-decay brief: the concept is present via fading labels, but the system isn't polished into a multi-channel, cohesive decay language.
